purpose: Stress-test proposition-level lineage inside an officially mapped provision that the successor correlation table labels 'amended'. The fixture demonstrates that one provision-to-provision structural edge can contain both continuing propositions and newly introduced propositions.

official_structural_evidence.observation: Article 11 of Directive 92/34/EEC maps to Article 9 of Directive 2008/90/EC with the explicit qualifier 'amended'.

authentic_text_comparison.rationale: Both authentic provisions retain the operative gate that propagating material and fruit plants may be marketed only in sufficiently homogeneous lots and when qualified/documented as CAC or certified categories. Terminology and implementing references change, so this claim is deliberately narrower than whole-article identity.
Both texts preserve the rule allowing labelling requirements for retail supply to a non-professional final consumer to be confined to appropriate product information.

The successor Article 9 contains a distinct genetically-modified-variety label/document disclosure obligation for which Article 11 of the predecessor text contains no corresponding proposition. This is not evidence that every part of Article 9 is novel; it is evidence against whole-provision semantic identity.

architecture_result.decision: Rule lineage is proposition-granular and may fan in/out beneath a single structural provision edge.
architecture_result.invariant: A provision-level qualifier such as 'amended' is a warning against whole-provision semantic continuity, not a verdict that all predecessor propositions terminated. Structural correspondence must be decomposed into independently evidenced rule anchors before semantic lineage is emitted.
forbidden_shortcuts: Treat Article 11 -> Article 9 amended as one RULE_CONTINUES claim covering the entire provisions.
Treat the qualifier amended as proof that every predecessor proposition terminated.
Assign the new GMO disclosure proposition an invented predecessor merely because it resides in the structural successor provision.

source_notes: EUR-Lex authentic Directive 92/34/EEC Article 11 contains the homogeneous-lot/qualification rule and retail non-professional labelling relaxation.
EUR-Lex authentic Directive 2008/90/EC Article 9 retains those propositions and additionally contains paragraph 3 on genetically modified varieties.
Consolidated texts may be used as verification checkpoints, but this fixture's lineage claims are anchored to the original legal acts and their official correlation table.
